findings.finding: The plan describes validating and documenting the trivial one-command closure, but does not identify the writer change that records the default row. Keeping the existing CLI permissive does not itself implement this behavior. Without that change, trivial records could newly fail F11 while still requiring users to populate individual review types.
findings.suggestion: Specify the writer command and persisted representation for the single `trivial-auto` default. Add a CLI round-trip proving that recording `self` and the default closes the remaining types without seven individual codes, and that the default cannot satisfy `self`.

findings.finding: Step 1 says each skipped row needs a `reason_code`, but does not explicitly require that code to be valid for that review type from `small` upward. Global vocabulary membership alone would allow a legitimate code on an inappropriate type; adding `no-spawn-site` makes its permitted scope particularly important.
findings.suggestion: Explicitly validate type/code compatibility using the shared vocabulary. Define where `no-spawn-site` is allowed, and test unknown codes, valid codes attached to the wrong type, and rejection of `trivial-auto` at every complexity above trivial.

findings.finding: Adding completed `self` rows to existing fixtures can mask whether all-`not_run` records actually fail across the full complexity range—the central regression this unit must prevent. The test outline does not explicitly preserve that negative case.
findings.suggestion: Add a parameterized all-`not_run` rejection test for every supported complexity, independent of the background-row helper. Include missing `self`, completed `self` without evidence, and the accepted trivial default-row case. Tag tests from their first commit, run pytest roots separately, and include `uv run scripts/verify_local.py` before push.  The gate changes and ledger extraction are directionally sound and proportionate. Clarify the default-row writer path, enforce per-type code validity, and make the central regression cases explicit before implementation proceeds.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise

findings.finding: The docs state "rows in already-merged records are legacy and are never re-verified," but `reason_codes_closed` has no cutoff — it fails any `not_run`/`not_applicable` row without a `reason_code`, including rows written before this change. Since `_no_entry_detail` (in `_entry_details.py`) explicitly contemplates re-verifying older runs from the tree, re-running F11 on any pre-U3 run whose rows are within the retention window will now fail on legacy codeless rows — contradicting the documented contract.
findings.suggestion: Either gate `reason_codes_closed` on a cutoff (e.g. skip rows whose run predates this change, or consult the `commit_hash` param already threaded into `check_review_record`), or soften the doc claim to "the current F11 run is not re-run on merged records."

findings.finding: The docs say from `small` up "each type names its OWN code" (e.g. `plan_internal` → `complexity-below-threshold`), but the enforcement only checks (a) a code is present and (b) it isn't `trivial-auto`. A uniform `close-missing --reason-code diff-below-threshold` applied to all seven types — including `plan` and `external_code`, for which the docs prescribe other codes — passes the gate. The tests themselves rely on this (`test_record_review_pass_cli_floor._close_missing` defaults every type to `diff-below-threshold` at small and asserts `.ok`), so the enforced contract is weaker than the documented one.
findings.suggestion: Either add a per-type code map to `reason_codes_closed` (at least for the types with an unambiguous code), or state in the docs that any non-`trivial-auto` code is accepted from small up.

findings.finding: test_an_evidence_free_self_row_fails` uses `make_entry("self", "completed", recorded_by="none")`. Whether this actually fails depends on `carries_evidence` treating the literal string `"none"` as non-evidence — a magic value not documented in the diff. If `carries_evidence` only checks non-blankness, this test would fail for the wrong reason (or the implementation needs a special case). Worth pinning the intended semantics.
findings.suggestion: Either record the self row with `recorded_by=None` (the actual "nobody earned it" shape the module docstring describes) or document that `"none"` is a recognized null adapter in `carries_evidence`.

findings.finding: When the `self` row is absent entirely, `entry_for(record, "self")` presumably yields an empty/pending row; if the earlier pending check does not materialize `self` as pending (it was described as materialized "up front" for live runs, but hand-built fixtures may omit it), `self_review_recorded` reports `` `self` is '' `` — a confusing empty-status message. Minor, but the message should distinguish "absent" from a status.
findings.suggestion: Branch on an absent row and say "`self` has no row" before formatting the status.  Everything else checks out: the extraction from `iterate_checks.py` preserves the public import surface (and a test pins it), the ledger trivial-row logic correctly refuses `trivial-auto` above trivial and accepts justification-or-enumeration at trivial, `close-missing`-cannot-complete-self is exercised, campaign roundtrip tests were updated with the new codes, and new tests are tagged `pytest.mark.covers` per the campaign contract. No security issues introduced — all inputs are file-backed JSON validated against closed vocabularies.  Overall: ship-with-fixes — the core U3 behavior is correctly implemented and well-tested; the doc-vs-enforcement gaps above (especially the legacy-record promise) should be reconciled before merge.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
